scenario: Satellite-based SO₂ sensors only record volcanic flux events exceeding 60 kt/day (detection sensitivity limit). Recorded events show a mean flux of 92 kt/day (σ=18 kt/day). Volcanologists need the true mean SO₂ flux across all eruptive events.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming SO₂ flux follows a normal distribution with σ=18 kt/day, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 60] = 92. (b) What fraction of all SO₂ flux events lie above the 60 kt/day threshold? (c) By how much (in kt/day) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 92 kt/day is E[X|X>60], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=92 numerically yields μ=90.14651 kt/day. Only 95.3% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 1.85349 kt/day. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean SO₂ flux is 92 kt/day because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 60 kt/day are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>60], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=60, σ=18. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 92 and solve for μ via brentq on [-390.0, 91.9999]. (4) Solution: μ=90.14651 kt/day. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((60−90.14651)/18)=0.95301.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 92,18,60
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-90.14651)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.95301)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-1.85349)<0.01
